reviews.name: v1-fresh-opus-review

actualProcess.scope: Fresh nonauthor review of exact v1 HTML/React security/evidence wording and disclosure wiring as an explanatory proposed draft; no protocol/production/native approval.

recommendation.scope: Only the exact security and evidence wording, disclosure wiring and security-relevant frontend behaviour of the v1 explanatory PROPOSED page draft (index.html requested hash f5aa9fceb5a0ff4c174617aa7bbd7bbf73a51866e6829bee5f4dde83637eab9d, hash not verified by this reviewer), its React source and generated data. Not cryptographic approval, Moriarty execution, production, publication authority, or setup, native, ledger, wallet or operator readiness.
recommendation.firstBlockedBoundary: Exact security wording of v1: fix F-01 (stray "0" in the DR-04 assembled status), F-02 (lifecycle liveness and issuance-card disclosure) and F-03 (render the complete retained broader scope). Then produce a new HTML version and get a fresh exact-byte Opus wording review. F-04 to F-06 should be fixed in the same pass.
recommendation.ordinarySelftestScope: none; nothing was built, run, rendered or tested

findings.summary: A stray literal "0" corrupts the DR-04 assembled-state security string. The page starts in this state for every case.
findings.evidence:
In versions/v1/app/src/App.jsx, Explorer, the `.assembly-status` div (role=status, aria-live=polite, data-testid=assembly-status) contains `{omitted.length&&

On the issuance route, …

}`. The inline bundle in versions/v1/index.html has the same expression: `i.length&&s.default.createElement("p",null,"On the issuance route…")`. When omitted.length===0, React renders the number 0 as text, so the status reads "…roles shown. Not proof verification, not acceptance, not settlement.0". omitted starts as [] and is reset to [] on every case change, so this is the default rendering. It is a deterministic React behaviour from the source; I did not observe it in a browser. DR-04 (SECURITY-COPY.json /diagramRules/3/rule) requires that exact text, and the integration rule says to quote exactly.
findings.requiredFix:
In App.jsx, change only the condition to `omitted.length>0&&

…

`. Rebuild the bundle, which changes the same expression in index.html. No wording changes.

findings.summary: The lifecycle section's V2 issuance-route description cites ERR-06 but leaves out its "safe but not live" orphaning caveat, and has no one-step disclosure to the issuance-route card.
findings.evidence: The lifecycle section (App.jsx `lifecycle` array and Lifecycle(); index.html `ug`/`og`) describes Produce, Issue and Consume. Consume reads: "Settlement consumes claim outputs, recomputes statements and requires each claimant’s signature and token burn." The drawer "Issuance funding, release & the alternative design" covers min-ADA, early reclaim and proof-at-consumption, then lists "Opus ERR-04 / ERR-06 / ERR-12 / ERR-25". It never states the ERR-06 content: any catalogue account may Revoke, and a competing settlement may spend the outref, orphaning issued claims and locking their value until expiry. That caveat appears only in SECURITY-COPY.json /cards/4/assumptions/1, inside the separate evidence section. There it is several disclosures and a section away, not adjacent or one disclosure away as the integrationRule and learning securityScope displayRule require for a V2 description. Readers of the lifecycle could assume issued claims will reliably be consumed.
findings.requiredFix: Smallest fix: in the lifecycle drawer, add a link to `#security-card-issuance-route` with the same onClick-open behaviour as the FAQ disclosure links, labelled "Full Opus scope & assumptions". Alternatively, quote /cards/4/assumptions/1 exactly with the card's evidenceStage. Change no other lifecycle wording.

findings.summary: The rendered broader-scope list is incomplete but reads as complete. The prepared learning.broaderScope content (general financial obligations, ACTUS, DeFi, bounded multiparent PCD) is never rendered.
findings.evidence: In App.jsx Evidence(), the drawer "Correspondence, broader scope & evidence limits" says: "Universal certificates, authenticated history, recursion, private handoff and multiparent composition remain required tracks." data.generated.json /learning/broaderScope (sourced from S07 /allRequiredScopeRetained and CONCEPT.md "Evidence appendix and retained breadth") also lists "General financial obligations" and "Bounded multiparent PCD", ACTUS (277 fixtures, 18 executable types, 32 taxonomy dispositions, DS01–07) and DeFi (72 rows, DA01–24, held-outs, intent cases, regressions). App.jsx never references `broaderScope`, so none of this appears on the page. Card 1 covers the 20 families, the 235 IDs, 42/52 and Midnight. The general financial obligations track and the ACTUS and DeFi corpora appear nowhere visible.
findings.requiredFix: In that same drawer, render data.learning.broaderScope verbatim: body, familiesStatus, furtherTracks, actus, defi, target, qualification, catalogue. Alternatively, extend the existing sentence to name every furtherTracks entry and the ACTUS and DeFi retention. Do not reword or narrow any item.

findings.summary: The noscript evidence paraphrase leaves out operator forgeability and the statement that no on-chain transaction is recorded.
findings.evidence: The index.html <noscript> says: "Recorded results are limited local proof and compiled-wrapper observations under a single-party test setup with caller-fabricated contexts." The exact Opus maturity text (SECURITY-COPY.json /maturity/body) reads "a single-party test setup whose operator can forge proofs" and "No on-chain transaction is recorded." The noscript sentence is new security wording, not an exact quote.
findings.requiredFix: Replace the noscript evidence sentence with the exact /maturity/body string. Minimal alternative: insert "whose operator can forge proofs" after "single-party test setup" and add "No on-chain transaction is recorded."

findings.summary: Rendered sourceRefs show pointers without the document they point into, which weakens evidence traceability.
findings.evidence: Generation dropped the `path` fields (compare contributions/04-scenarios/invoice-fixtures.json and 08-learning/learning.json with data.generated.json). The Sources drawers therefore show bare pointers such as "Two-order allocation target · /11", "Pool rounding target · /9" and "CL-20 · /claims/19", with no S02, CLAIMS-REGISTER or SECURITY-ERRATA document named.
findings.requiredFix: In data generation, keep a short document identifier (for example "S02-PATTERN-INVENTORY.json" or "CLAIMS-REGISTER.json") and render it with each pointer in Sources(). No copy change.

findings.summary: Two exact-quote FAQs appear without the sourceRefs of the rule they quote. Some quoted rule texts read as instructions to authors.
findings.evidence: In data.generated.json /learning/faq, "partial-range" quotes SECURITY-COPY.json /invoiceRules/1/rule and "strand" quotes /glossaryClarifications/0. Neither shows the rule's sourceRefs ("S12 action partial"; CL-04, ERR-28, A04 /glossary), and neither has a disclosure link. FAQs that do have a disclosure link point to cards whose refs differ from those of the quoted rule. Displayed answers include author directives such as "Label it PROPOSED application policy." and "Never show closed, complete or reserve returned." These are faithful quotes, but they are oddly framed for readers.
findings.requiredFix: Below each EXACT_OPUS_QUOTE FAQ answer, show the quoted Opus item's own sourceRefs, for example refs(rule.sourceRefs). Keep the quotes byte-exact. Any rephrasing for readers needs an Opus referral.

findings.summary: Two aria-live regions announce the same omission state.
findings.evidence: WebDiagram.jsx `.web-diagram__state` has aria-live=polite and stays visible. App.jsx `.assembly-status` has role=status and aria-live=polite. Screen readers will announce every toggle twice. This is an accessibility issue, not a wording one.
findings.requiredFix: Remove aria-live from `.web-diagram__state`, or hide that element visually and from AT. The app status is the authoritative text.

findings.summary: Unreachable fallback copy and an unused learning item carry unreviewed or stage-upgraded wording.
findings.evidence: Fallbacks in App.jsx: `data.maturity` (short maturity text without "operator can forge proofs" or "No on-chain transaction is recorded"), `faqs`, `journeys`, and the evidence-grid fallback. They are unreachable with the current inlined data. learning.evidence["current-record"] labels the whole maturity body stage "RECORDED", even though that body contains V2 readings and the conditional argument. It is not rendered.
findings.requiredFix: Before any future wiring, remove the fallbacks or replace them with the exact Opus strings. Do not render current-record with stage RECORDED; use per-claim stage labels instead.

findings.summary: Minor vocabulary: the inspector calls a planned role an "illustrated Strand" or "illustrated proof".
findings.evidence: App.jsx inspector: aria-label="Selected illustrated Strand" and the checkbox text "Omit this illustrated proof". The glossary says "planned proof role … is not a Strand". The "illustrated Strand" phrasing does come from Opus's own DR-01 and glossaryClarifications/9, and the subtitle clarifies that this is "An explanation control, not a transaction action."
findings.requiredFix: Optional: "Selected illustrated role" / "Omit this illustrated role". Not required for readiness.
